text: Outcome grading: check the world, not the claim Anthropic's vocabulary is the clearest available: a task is one test with inputs and success criteria, a trial is one attempt at it, a grader scores some aspect of the attempt, the transcript (or trajectory) is "the complete record of a trial, including outputs, tool calls, reasoning, intermediate results", and the outcome is "the final state in the environment at the end of the trial" ( Demystifying evals for AI agents ).

text: Outcome graders come in four common shapes: Shape How it decides Example State diff Replay the gold actions on a copy of the starting state, compare with the state the agent left τ²-bench hashes the agent's database and the gold database and requires equality ( evaluator_env.py ): any order of calls, any wording, the same end state Tests Run tests the agent's change must make pass, and tests it must not break SWE-bench's FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS test lists ( SWE-bench harness ); Terminal-Bench's tests/test.sh writing 1 or 0 (its isolation problem is on Agentic benchmarks ) Assertions Programmatic checks on named parts of the state τ²-bench telecom's environment assertions on the simulated phone; OSWorld's per-task checker scripts Required information String checks that the agent told the user specific facts τ²-bench's communicate_info : a substring that must appear in an agent message A state diff is the strongest of these because it is indifferent to path and wording, and it sees changes the agent never mentioned.
